entities.summary: The Ulm campaign was a series of French and Bavarian military maneuvers and battles to outflank and capture an Austrian army in 1805 during the War of the Third Coalition. It took place in the vicinity of and inside the Swabian city of Ulm. The French Grande Armée, led by Emperor Napoleon, had 210,000 troops organized into seven corps and hoped to knock out the Austrian army in the Danube before Russian reinforcements could arrive. Rapid marching let Napoleon conduct a large wheeling maneuver, which captured an Austrian army of 60,000 under Feldmarschall-Leutnant (FML) Karl Freiherr Mack von Leiberich on 20 October at Ulm.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Ulm campaign was a pivotal battle in Napoleon's War of the Third Coalition, where French forces decisively defeated an Austrian army of 60,000 under Feldmarschall-Leutnant Karl Freiherr Mack von Leiberich on October 20, 1805. This victory allowed Napoleon to control the Danube and set the stage for his subsequent victories at Austerlitz and Jena.
